parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain how redshift leads to the idea that the Universe is expanding.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Stars in a distant galaxy emit radiation. The total luminosity of the stars in the galaxy is 1.90 × 10³⁶ W.
The emission spectrum of the radiation contains a line X at a wavelength of 658 nm.

Radiation from the galaxy is observed on the Earth. The observed radiation has a radiant flux intensity of 8.42 × 10⁻¹⁶ W m⁻². In the observed emission spectrum, line X is at a wavelength of 726 nm.

Determine:
parts.text: the distance *d* of the galaxy from the Earth

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the speed *v* of the galaxy relative to the Earth.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: Observations of many galaxies, such as the one in (b), lead to many pairs of values of *d* and *v*. Plotting these values reveals a trend.
parts.text:
On Fig. 10.1, sketch the variation of *v* with *d*.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of the quantity represented by the gradient of the line in Fig. 10.1.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.1
figures.alt: Blank set of axes with *v* on the vertical axis and *d* on the horizontal axis, both marked zero and ending in arrowheads.
